title: UAE, Jordan Face Largest Share Of Jobs At Risk From AI In Middle East, Says World Bank
source_used: Khaleej Times (read on its Menafn copy)
key_facts: The share of jobs at risk of being substituted by AI is largest in the UAE and Jordan and smallest in Afghanistan and Pakistan, per the World Bank's October Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (Menaap) Economic Update.
High-income economies face the most exposure because more of their jobs are cognitive occupations suited to generative AI.
Across the region the risk of substitution covers no more than about 10 per cent of jobs; 13 to 20 per cent have potential for AI to raise productivity, which the bank says “is far from guaranteed”.
The UAE shows above-average AI use in 9 of 22 occupation groups.

The estimate draws on one million Claude conversations published by Anthropic; the bank cautions these users may be more educated and knowledge-intensive than the wider population, which could overstate the gains.
Since ChatGPT's launch, the value of jobs in the most AI-substitutable freelance skills has fallen 9.8 per cent and new entrants have dropped 12.1 per cent, versus the least exposed skills.
Only 16 per cent of firms in the region introduced a new product or service in the past three years, against 29 per cent in other emerging markets.

why_it_matters_hint: Official World Bank figures put a ceiling of about 10% on AI replacement risk in the region, with rich Gulf economies most exposed.
